title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce per-token inference cost by providing an automated defaults/autotune layer that sets batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles per-model and per-workload plus an accompanying unit-economics tooling surface in the Console. Changes: 1) runtime/autotune service that profiles traffic and suggests stable defaults (target_latency, batch_size, cache_ttl, quant_profile). 2) new quantization profiles (int8/ptq/per-channel heuristics) added to model-registry and runtime kernel-selection. 3) API: new proposal endpoint POST /v1/autotune/suggest and enforcement flag enable_autotune_defaults in inference configs. 4) Console: Unit Economics dashboard tab showing estimated cost-per-request with before/after projections and rollout controls for applying autotuned defaults. 5) Telemetry: additional tagging for autotune decisions + opt-in privacy-safe export. 6) Migrations: DB migration + config schema bump (v3->v4). Testing: added integration tests for batcher fallback, KV cache warmup, quantized execution correctness, and end-to-end unit-econ projections. Backwards compatibility: defaults are opt-in via enable_autotune_defaults=false by default; rollout documented. See linked Linear tickets for roadmap and PM notes.
commits: init: add autotune service scaffold and API endpoints
runtime: implement batcher scoring and cache_ttl heuristics
model-registry: quant profiles and selection logic
telemetry: add autotune decision events and opt-in flag
tests: integration tests for batching/caching/quantization e2e
diff_snippets: + func (p *Profiler) SuggestBatchSize(stats TrafficStats) int { return clamp(int(stats.avgSeq/16), 1, 256) }

+ quant_profiles:
- name: int8-paq-v2
  backend: fbgemm
  params: "per_channel=true"
ci_checks: perf-benchmarks: flaky -> rerun -> pass (throughput +4% on typical chat workload)
review_comments: Liam Chen: Could you include the perf numbers that motivated the defaults and show distribution across seq lengths?

Ava Martinez: Added benchmark table in docs and uploaded raw CSVs to the Linear task; saw median p50 latency drop ~8% and cost per 1M tokens down ~12% with autotuned defaults on our standard chat load.
Priya Kapoor: Please ensure telemetry only includes aggregated signals and is behind the opt-in flag; also confirm no PII is captured.
Ava Martinez: Telemetry is aggregated counts/histograms only; events include model_id, seq_len_bucket, and chosen_profile but not prompt text. Opt-in flag defaults to false in config.
Diego Alvarez: DB migration looks fine but add a downgrade path and a safe rollout strategy in case of regressions.
Ava Martinez: Added migration downgrade and a migration-runbook in docs/migration-notes.md. Also added a canary rollout policy in Console rollout controls.
author_replies: Thanks for the reviews — addressed feedback from Priya and Diego, added perf tables and downgrade path. Left enable_autotune_defaults as opt-in to avoid unexpected changes for existing customers.
merge_commit_message:
cost(autotune): add autotune defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling

- runtime autotune profiler & suggestions API
- quantization profiles in model-registry
- Console: Unit Economics dashboard and rollout controls
- telemetry events (opt-in)
- DB migration + tests
release_notes: Added an optional autotune defaults feature that suggests and can apply batching, cache TTL, and quantization profiles per model to reduce inference unit cost. Console includes a Unit Economics dashboard to preview cost impact. Opt-in by default; see docs/migration-notes.md for rollout steps.
